text:
Utah hosts Pittsburgh tonight with a slight edge in the model, which projects UTA to score 3.32 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to PIT's 3.07. Five on five, the two are close, with PIT at 55% of the expected goals in its games and UTA at 56%. The gap is at the back end: UTA allows 2.71 expected goals per 60 minutes against 3.48 for PIT. On special teams, UTA's power play (0.84 expected goals per game) and penalty kill (0.49 allowed) both beat PIT's (0.53 and 0.71). UTA does take 4.4 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays.

In net, the projected starters are Arturs Silovs for PIT and Karel Vejmelka for UTA. Neither is having a good fall. Goals saved above expected measures how many more goals a goalie stopped than an average one would have on the same shots. Silovs is at -0.15 over five games, after -12.76 across 39 games last season. Vejmelka is at -1.29 this year, though he was +5.39 over 64 games last season. He has struggled lately, with a .857 save percentage and 3.5 goals worse than expected over his last five starts.

On form, PIT is 1-3-1 in its last five with 48% of the expected goals, while UTA is 3-2-0 with 57%. The Penguins close a four-game road trip, are 0-3-0 on it, and are playing their third game in four nights, though the model doesn't price that. Rickard Rakell has no goals in nine games on 3.0 expected goals and is flagged as due, with a 28% chance to score tonight. Utah's Nick Schmaltz and Dylan Guenther each sit at 33%.
